title: Flat constant extension and K-flat tensor of pro-zero cone towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $R=\underline A$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $R\to\mathcal O$ a flat map of commutative ring sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For an $A$-complex $X$, put $E(X)=\mathcal O\otimes_R\underline X$, termwise. Let $v_n:X_n\to Y_n$ be a strict map of inverse sequences of $A$-complexes, whose cone tower is pro-zero in $D(A)$: for every $n$, some transition $\operatorname{Cone}(v_m)\to\operatorname{Cone}(v_n)$, $m\geq n$, is zero. Use derived categories and mapping cones [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor and total tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every possibly unbounded K-flat $\mathcal O$-complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], the strict map
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal O}E(X_\bullet)\longrightarrow P\otimes_{\mathcal O}E(Y_\bullet)$$
has a pro-zero cone tower in $D(\mathcal O)$ and induces an isomorphism on total right derived inverse limits of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. If compatible chain maps $A[0]\to X_n,Y_n$ make $v_n$ commute with their units, that isomorphism carries the induced map $P\to R\lim(P\otimes E(X_n))$ to $P\to R\lim(P\otimes E(Y_n))$. These maps are the strict cones followed by the K-injective derived-limit comparison, not independently chosen maps in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), transport of the Koszul pro-isomorphism; general flat constant-extension and tensor argument extracted by NE.

proof.text: The constant module sheaf functor $M\mapsto\underline M$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact], whose statement applies to every module over every commutative ring, without finite-generation hypotheses. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], tensoring with the flat $R$-module $\mathcal O$ is exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. The tensor has its usual $\mathcal O$-action, so its value is $E(M)$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves kernels and cokernels and is faithful [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. It therefore detects exactness: a homology object with zero underlying sheaf is zero, since faithfulness detects its zero identity. Thus $E:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is an exact additive functor.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functor $E$ of Step 1. Its termwise functor on unbounded complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $E_D:D(A)\to D(\mathcal O)$ with a natural comparison $E_DQ_A\cong Q_{\mathcal O}E$. It sends the zero object to zero, as $E(0)=0$. A zero morphism factors through the zero object, so $E_D$ sends zero morphisms to zero. In particular no choice of a null homotopy for a map zero only in $D(A)$ is needed.

Put $T(B)=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}B$ with the direct-sum total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. If $f:B\to B'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $C(f)$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. The definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $C(f)\otimes P$ acyclic. The signed interchange $p\otimes c\mapsto(-1)^{ij}c\otimes p$ in bidegree $(i,j)$ identifies $P\otimes C(f)$ with $C(f)\otimes P$: the two differential components agree using $(-1)^{(i+1)j}=(-1)^{ij+j}$ and $(-1)^{i(j+1)}=(-1)^{ij+i}$. This is a map on the direct sums with its inverse given by the same signs. The natural tensor-cone isomorphism [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] identifies $P\otimes C(f)$ with $C(T(f))$. Thus $C(T(f))$ is acyclic, and the same cone criterion makes $T(f)$ a quasi-isomorphism. This uses K-flatness alone, with no hypothesis on the individual terms of $P$.

The complex functor $Q_{\mathcal O}T$ now inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the localization of complexes defining $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It supplies $T_D:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ and a natural isomorphism $T_DQ_{\mathcal O}\cong Q_{\mathcal O}T$. Since $T(0)=0$, this comparison at the zero complex shows that $T_D$ sends the zero object to zero and hence sends every zero morphism to zero by its factorization through that object. Composing the comparisons of Steps 2 and 4 gives a natural identification $(T_DE_D)Q_A\cong Q_{\mathcal O}TE$.

source.place: Section 05RR, Definition 05RU: localization at quasi-isomorphisms; categories.tex Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization).

proof.text:
Write $C_n=C(v_n)$ and $w_n=T(E(v_n))$. The cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is $C(v_n)^r=Y_n^r\oplus X_n^{r+1}$ with differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_Y&v_n\\0&-d_X\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Since $E$ is additive, applying it gives $E(C_n)\cong C(E(v_n))$, with the same matrix after applying $E$ to each entry. A strictly commuting square with vertical maps $a:X_m\to X_n$, $b:Y_m\to Y_n$ has cone map $\operatorname{diag}(b,a[1])$; the biproduct comparison just described commutes with this map. Next use the natural isomorphism of [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] for the fixed complex $P$. Consequently
$$\theta_n:T(E(C_n))\xrightarrow{\sim}C(w_n)$$
is natural for every strict tower transition. In particular these are isomorphisms of strict towers, not unrelated isomorphisms at individual levels.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), Tag 014F (lemma-functorial-cone) for strictly commuting squares; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact).

proof.text: Fix $n$ and choose $m\geq n$ such that the given transition $c_{mn}:C_m\to C_n$ has $Q_A(c_{mn})=0$. Steps 2 and 4 give $(T_DE_D)(Q_A(c_{mn}))=0$. By their natural comparisons, this says $Q_{\mathcal O}(TE(c_{mn}))=0$. The naturality in Step 5 identifies the transition $C(w_m)\to C(w_n)$ with $\theta_n\circ TE(c_{mn})\circ\theta_m^{-1}$, so its localization is zero as well. This proves the required pro-zero property with the very same $m$ as for the original cone tower. If $m=n$, the hypothesis says that $C_n$ is a zero object and the argument still applies.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), transport of the pro-isomorphism: explicit application of the localized functors and natural cone comparison.

proof.text:
Let $Z_\bullet=TE(X_\bullet)$ and $W_\bullet=TE(Y_\bullet)$, with strict map $w:Z_\bullet\to W_\bullet$. By Step 6 its strict cone tower is pro-zero in $D(\mathcal O)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] on the given small site with coefficient ring sheaf $\mathcal O$. It states precisely that the canonical map
$$u=R\lim(w):R\lim Z_\bullet\longrightarrow R\lim W_\bullet$$
is an isomorphism. This is the total right derived functor on the category of strict towers; the cited statement does not require exactness of countable products, boundedness of the complexes, or a uniform bound on the zero transitions.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); pro-zero consequence as stated in the cited strict-tower theorem.

proof.text: Suppose the unit chain maps are given. The tensor unit identifications $E(A[0])=\mathcal O[0]$ and $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O[0]\cong P$ are degreewise multiplication, with inverse $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Applying $TE$ to the given maps produces strict maps $\alpha:\Delta P\to Z_\bullet$, $\beta:\Delta P\to W_\bullet$ with $w\alpha=\beta$ as chain maps. To check the specified derived-limit maps, choose tower K-injective resolutions $j_Z:Z_\bullet\to I$, $j_W:W_\bullet\to J$ computing the total derived functor as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The canonical maps from $P$ are the localizations of $\lim(j_Z\alpha):P=\lim\Delta P\to\lim I$ and $\lim(j_W\beta):P\to\lim J$.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits) and Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective computation applied to the strict coaugmentations; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK (section-tensor-product).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] in the abelian category of strict $\mathcal O$-module towers to the K-injective target $J$. Represent the derived map $Q(j_W)Q(w)Q(j_Z)^{-1}:QI\to QJ$ by a chain map $h:I\to J$. Injectivity of the same Hom comparison for source $Z_\bullet$ says that $hj_Z$ and $j_Ww$ are homotopic as tower maps. Composing this tower homotopy with $\alpha$ gives a homotopy from $hj_Z\alpha$ to $j_W\beta$. Termwise inverse limit preserves that homotopy: applying its additive functor to $f-g=dH+Hd$ gives the identical equation for $\lim H$. Thus
$$Q(\lim h)\,Q(\lim(j_Z\alpha))=Q(\lim(j_W\beta)).$$
By the K-injective computation of the total derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $Q(\lim h)$ is the map $R\lim(w)=u$ of Step 7 under these resolution comparisons. The equality therefore proves that this particular isomorphism carries the specified unit for $X_\bullet$ to the specified unit for $Y_\bullet$. No map between abstract triangulated cones has been selected.
